evidence.estrutura: Mernissi analyzed social and gender power rather than constitutional territorial design; no strong centralization/federalism doctrine.
evidence.representacao: Her scholarship emphasized women’s participation, public voice and democratic possibilities in Muslim societies.
evidence.poder: Critique of patriarchal authority and social control supports individual autonomy and limits on coercive hierarchy.
evidence.imigracao: Her cross-cultural scholarship and critique of rigid identity boundaries support pluralism, though migration law was not central.
evidence.diplomacia: Her work was intellectual and cross-cultural rather than military; a diplomatic/internationalist orientation is more plausible than militarism.
evidence.intervencao: Anti-domination and postcolonial analysis support skepticism toward external coercion and imperial intervention.
evidence.economia: Her sociology addressed social inequality but did not define a comprehensive market-versus-public ownership model; moderate-left.
evidence.controle: No evidence for command planning; moderate regulatory/social-state orientation.
evidence.comercio: No distinctive trade doctrine is established.
evidence.religiao: She re-read Islamic texts and history to challenge patriarchal interpretations; reformist/secularizing but not anti-Islamic.
evidence.moral: Feminist scholarship on gender hierarchy and autonomy strongly supports progressive social positions.
evidence.tecnologia: Modern sociology and education suggest pragmatic modernism, not a distinct technology ideology.
